header.running_head: The Importance Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) Gave to the Adhaan

blocks.text: immediately climbed up a date palm and called out the Adhaan. "What made you call out the Adhaan, O Sa'd?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) replied, "May my parents be sacrificed for you! I saw you with only a handful of people and did not see Bilaal (RA) with you. When I then noticed the slaves looking at each other and then at you, I feared that they would harm you, so I called out the Adhaan (so that other Muslims would come quickly)." "You did the right thing, O Sa'd," Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Whenever you see Bilaal not with me, you should call out the Adhaan." Thereafter, Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) called out the Adhaan thrice during Rasulullaah ﷺ's lifetime. [^1]
Statements of the Sahabah (RA) Concerning the Adhaan and the People who Call out the Adhaan

Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) said, "The share (of rewards) of those who call out the Adhaan on the Day of Qiyaamah will be like the share of those who wage Jihaad. During the time between the Adhaan and the Iqaamah, the Mu'adhin is like the martyr tossing and turning in his blood in the path of Allaah."
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "If I were a Mu'adhin, I care not whether I perform Hajj or Umrah or wage Jihaad."

Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) said, "If I were a Mu'adhin, my affairs would have been perfected and I care not whether I woke up for (Nafl) salaah during the night or whether I fasted (Nafl fasts) during the day because I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ pray, 'O Allaah! Forgive those who call out the Adhaan. O Allaah! Forgive those who call out the Adhaan.' 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' I said, 'But (why do you emphasise calling out the Adhaan so much when) you have left us in a condition that we would draw swords to call out the Adhaan?' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'That is not the case, O Umar because there will soon come a time when people will leave the Adhaan to the weak ones amongst them. The flesh that is forbidden for Jahannam is the flesh of those who call out the Adhaan.'"
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) mentioned that it is the Mu'adhin to whom Allaah refers in the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: وَمَنْ اَحْسَنُ قَوْلًا مِّمَّنْ دَعَاۤ اِلَى اللّٰهِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا وَّقَالَ اِنَّنِيْ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِيْنَ
blocks.text: Whose speech can be better than the one who calls (others) towards Allaah, who performs righteous deeds, and (humbly) says, "I am from the Muslims (from those who submit to Allaah)."

She says further, "The Mu'adhin calls towards Allaah when he says 'حَيَّ عَلَى الصَّلٰوةِ' ('Come to salaah'), he performs a righteous deed when he performs the salaah and he is certainly amongst the Muslims when he says, 'لَا اِلٰهَ اِلَّا اللّٰهُ' ('There is none worthy of worship but Allaah')." [^2]
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.336) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Bayhaqi in his Shu'abul Imaan, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.265). Abush Sheikh has reported similar narrations from Rasaafi in his Kitaabul Adhaan, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.266).
